evaluation.final_reason: Housemates agreed on immediate cleaning and ventilation norms but did not address the separate scheduling complaint. Concretely: Agent A committed to the behavioral change: 'I'll make sure to use the fan and clean up right after,' Agent B accepted ('Sounds good.'), Agent C asked for a group rule: 'can we all agree to wash the pan right after we use it from now on?' and Agent D assented: 'That works for me.' These lines show a mutual spoken agreement to wash the pan immediately and use the extractor fan. However, Agent D's earlier claim that 'it is impossible to use the stove on weeknights' was not discussed or settled, so some substantive disagreement remains.

substantive_insights: Lack of prior household rules created ambiguity about responsibility for shared cookware and ventilation; a simple behavioral rule (wash immediately/use fan) directly addresses both smell and cleanliness.
Mutual, explicit verbal commitments in a speech-only setting counted as settlement for the pan/ventilation issue: all four participants voiced acceptance.
A distinct practical demand (limiting or forbidding stove use on weeknights) was introduced but never negotiated, so partial resolution left an outstanding scheduling conflict.
